objectives.title: IaC
objectives.lesson: Declarative code describes the desired infrastructure state.

objectives.title: IaC benefits
objectives.lesson: Version control enables change review and repeatability.

objectives.title: Multi-cloud
objectives.lesson: Providers enable a common workflow across different APIs.

objectives.title: Provider versions
objectives.lesson: The lock file records selected provider versions.

objectives.title: Providers
objectives.lesson: A provider defines supported resources and data sources.

objectives.title: Multiple providers
objectives.lesson: An alias enables an alternative configuration of the same provider.

objectives.title: State
objectives.lesson: State maps resource addresses to real objects.

objectives.title: Workflow
objectives.lesson: Initialize a new working directory before planning and applying.

objectives.title: Init
objectives.lesson: Init prepares the backend, modules, and providers.

objectives.title: Validate
objectives.lesson: Validate checks syntax and internal consistency, not remote APIs.

objectives.title: Plan
objectives.lesson: Plan proposes changes. -out saves the plan.

objectives.title: Apply
objectives.lesson: Apply executes the proposed changes.

objectives.title: Destroy
objectives.lesson: Destroy removes managed objects.

objectives.title: Fmt
objectives.lesson: Fmt formats HCL; -check does not rewrite files.

objectives.title: Resources and data
objectives.lesson: A resource manages an object; data reads information.

objectives.title: References
objectives.lesson: A reference uses the resource type, name, and attribute.

objectives.title: Variables
objectives.lesson: An input variable is referenced using var.NAME.

objectives.title: Types
objectives.lesson: A set contains unique elements with no guaranteed order.

objectives.title: Expressions
objectives.lesson: Functions transform values; length returns the number of elements in a collection.

objectives.title: Lifecycle
objectives.lesson: Create_before_destroy changes replacement order; depends_on expresses a hidden dependency.

objectives.title: Conditions
objectives.lesson: A failed assertion in a check block produces a warning rather than blocking the operation.

objectives.title: Secrets
objectives.lesson: Sensitive hides values in output, not automatically in state. Ephemeral values are omitted from plans and state. Write-only arguments require provider support. Vault manages secrets.

objectives.title: Module sources
objectives.lesson: Modules can come from local paths, the Registry, or Git.

objectives.title: Scope
objectives.lesson: A child module receives inputs through the module block.

objectives.title: Module usage
objectives.lesson: Module outputs are referenced using module.NAME.OUTPUT.

objectives.title: Module versions
objectives.lesson: Argument version obmedzuje verziu registry modulu.

objectives.title: Local backend
objectives.lesson: The default backend is local, typically using terraform.tfstate.

objectives.title: Locking
objectives.lesson: State locking prevents conflicting concurrent writes.

objectives.title: Remote backend
objectives.lesson: The backend determines where state is stored. Use init -migrate-state to migrate it.

objectives.title: Drift
objectives.lesson: Refresh-only proposes updating state to match reality without repairing infrastructure. A moved block changes an address.

objectives.title: Import
objectives.lesson: Import associates an existing object with an address in state.

objectives.title: Inspect state
objectives.lesson: State list displays addresses; state show displays instance attributes.

objectives.title: Logging
objectives.lesson: TF_LOG sets logging verbosity; logs may contain secrets.

objectives.title: HCP runs
objectives.lesson: HCP Terraform supports remote runs and state management.

objectives.title: Governance
objectives.lesson: HCP supports policy enforcement, team permissions, and a private registry.

objectives.title: Projects
objectives.lesson: Projects group HCP workspaces. HCP workspaces are not the same as CLI workspaces.

objectives.title: Integration
objectives.lesson: The cloud block configures HCP integration; login obtains a token.

concepts.title: What does declarative IaC describe?
concepts.lesson: A declarative approach describes the desired state, not the sequence of every API call.

concepts.title: What is normally stored in .tf files?
concepts.lesson: HCL files define the desired infrastructure and its configuration.

concepts.title: Which approach explicitly describes steps to execute?
concepts.lesson: An imperative approach specifies individual steps; a declarative approach specifies the result.

concepts.title: What can Terraform compare with the desired configuration?
concepts.lesson: Terraform compares configuration, state, and object information.

concepts.title: What does an execution plan describe?
concepts.lesson: A plan proposes operations; it does not guarantee a successful apply.

concepts.title: Which practice enables peer review of infrastructure changes?
concepts.lesson: Git supports comparison, review, and configuration change history.

concepts.title: What helps reproduce similar environments?
concepts.lesson: Repeatable code reduces differences between environments.

concepts.title: What helps detect unintended changes before execution?
concepts.lesson: Reviewing a plan can reveal unexpected changes before apply.

concepts.title: What is a benefit of keeping infrastructure code in Git?
concepts.lesson: History tracks changes, but Git alone does not protect state.

concepts.title: What reduces repeated configuration across teams?
concepts.lesson: Modules reduce duplication and simplify standardization.

concepts.title: What connects Terraform to different cloud APIs?
concepts.lesson: Providers implement interfaces to individual services.

concepts.title: Can a single configuration use AWS and Azure providers?
concepts.lesson: One configuration can use multiple providers.

concepts.title: What is shared across different supported platforms?
concepts.lesson: Workflow commands are shared, but resource schemas differ.

concepts.title: What can a provider manage beyond public clouds?
concepts.lesson: Terraform is not limited to public clouds.

concepts.title: Does switching providers automatically translate every resource?
concepts.lesson: Resource types are provider-specific, and migration requires changes.

concepts.title: Which file records selected provider versions?
concepts.lesson: The lock file records provider versions and checksums.

concepts.title: Which block declares provider source and version constraints?
concepts.lesson: Required_providers belongs in the terraform block.

concepts.title: Which command can upgrade provider selections within constraints?
concepts.lesson: Init with -upgrade reselects versions within the constraints.

concepts.title: What does ~> 1.2.0 permit?
concepts.lesson: A three-component pessimistic constraint allows patch updates.

concepts.title: Should the dependency lock file normally be committed to Git?
concepts.lesson: Committing the lock file helps ensure consistent provider selection.

concepts.title: What exposes resource types to Terraform?
concepts.lesson: Provider implementuje resource a data source typy.

concepts.title: Which component communicates with a supported service API?
concepts.lesson: A plugin mediates operations against an external system.

concepts.title: What configures a provider region when supported?
concepts.lesson: A provider block configures settings such as region or authentication.

concepts.title: Does Terraform Core contain every AWS resource implementation?
concepts.lesson: Resource type implementations are provided by providers.

concepts.title: Which command shows provider requirements?
concepts.lesson: The command lists providers required by configuration and state.

concepts.title: What enables multiple configurations of the same provider?
concepts.lesson: An alias distinguishes alternative provider configurations.

concepts.title: How can a resource select an aliased AWS provider named west?
concepts.lesson: The provider meta-argument references a provider configuration.

concepts.title: Which provider configuration is used implicitly when available?
concepts.lesson: Without an explicit selection, the default configuration is used.

concepts.title: Which module argument maps provider configurations?
concepts.lesson: The providers map assigns provider configurations to a child module.

concepts.title: Can different aliases of one provider use different regions?
concepts.lesson: An alias allows you to manage two AWS regions, for example.

concepts.title: What is a primary purpose of Terraform state?
concepts.lesson: State binds configuration addresses to managed objects.

concepts.title: Can state contain confidential resource attributes?
concepts.lesson: State can contain sensitive data and must be protected.

concepts.title: Should two unrelated resource addresses manage the same remote object?
concepts.lesson: Terraform expects a unique mapping for each managed object.

concepts.title: What can Terraform use state metadata for?
concepts.lesson: State stores resource identity and other metadata.

concepts.title: What is the preferred way to modify state?
concepts.lesson: CLI operations reduce the risk of corrupting state.

concepts.title: Which sequence is typical for a new working directory?
concepts.lesson: Initialization prepares the directory before planning and applying.

concepts.title: Which phase defines desired infrastructure?
concepts.lesson: Configuration is the starting point of the workflow.

concepts.title: Which command previews changes?
concepts.lesson: Plan displays proposed changes.

concepts.title: Which command executes infrastructure changes?
concepts.lesson: Apply executes the approved plan.

concepts.title: Must a separate terraform plan command always precede interactive apply?
concepts.lesson: Apply without a saved plan creates its own plan.

concepts.title: Which command installs required providers?
concepts.lesson: Init prepares providers, modules, and the backend.

concepts.title: Does init normally create managed cloud resources?
concepts.lesson: Init prepares the working directory; it does not deploy declared resources.

concepts.title: Which init option ignores previously saved backend configuration?
concepts.lesson: Reconfigure initializes the backend without migrating existing state.

concepts.title: Where are downloaded provider plugins normally kept for a working directory?
concepts.lesson: The .terraform directory contains local working data.

concepts.title: Is rerunning init after a module source change appropriate?
concepts.lesson: Initialize dependencies after changing a module source.

concepts.title: Which command checks configuration consistency?
concepts.lesson: Validate checks syntax and internal consistency.

concepts.title: Does validate guarantee remote API permissions?
concepts.lesson: Validate does not check remote service availability or permissions.

concepts.title: Which init option prepares validation without accessing the configured backend?
concepts.lesson: Init -backend=false prepares modules and providers without initializing the backend.

concepts.title: Which validate option emits machine-readable output?
concepts.lesson: JSON output is suitable for automation.

concepts.title: What can validate detect?
concepts.lesson: The provider schema helps identify unsupported arguments.

concepts.title: Which option saves an execution plan?
concepts.lesson: Plan -out saves a binary plan for later apply.

concepts.title: What does a plus sign indicate in a normal plan?
concepts.lesson: The + symbol indicates resource creation.

concepts.title: What does plan -detailed-exitcode return when changes are present and planning succeeds?
concepts.lesson: Exit code 2 means a successful plan with changes; 1 means an error.

concepts.title: Can a saved plan contain sensitive values?
concepts.lesson: A saved plan may contain secrets in readable form.

concepts.title: Does normal terraform plan itself apply proposed resource changes?
concepts.lesson: Plan proposes changes; apply performs the deployment.

concepts.title: Which command executes a saved plan named planfile?
concepts.lesson: Apply accepts a saved plan as an argument.

concepts.title: What does -auto-approve skip for an automatically generated apply plan?
concepts.lesson: The flag skips confirmation, not authentication.

concepts.title: Can apply partially succeed before an error?
concepts.lesson: Some operations may succeed before a later operation fails.

concepts.title: What should be reviewed before applying changes?
concepts.lesson: A plan can reveal unwanted replacements or deletions.

concepts.title: Does applying a saved plan ask for normal interactive approval?
concepts.lesson: Passing a saved plan constitutes approval to execute it.

concepts.title: Which command removes managed infrastructure?
concepts.lesson: Destroy executes the removal of managed objects.

concepts.title: Which plan option previews destruction?
concepts.lesson: Plan -destroy prepares a destruction plan.

concepts.title: Does deleting local state automatically destroy remote resources?
concepts.lesson: Deleting state loses the mapping, not the remote objects themselves.

concepts.title: Which lifecycle rule rejects plans that would destroy a configured resource?
concepts.lesson: The rule protects against destructive plans while it remains in the configuration.

concepts.title: Should you inspect the destroy plan before approving it?
concepts.lesson: Review is especially important for production resources.

concepts.title: Which command checks formatting without rewriting files?
concepts.lesson: The -check flag checks formatting without rewriting files.

concepts.title: Which fmt option includes subdirectories?
concepts.lesson: Recursive formatting extends to subdirectories.

concepts.title: Which fmt option displays formatting differences?
concepts.lesson: The diff option displays formatting differences.

concepts.title: Does fmt validate cloud credentials?
concepts.lesson: Fmt changes HCL formatting, not cloud access.

concepts.title: Does ordinary terraform fmt rewrite files needing formatting?
concepts.lesson: By default, fmt writes formatted files.

concepts.title: Which block reads existing infrastructure information?
concepts.lesson: A data source reads information; a resource manages an object.

concepts.title: Which block declares a managed object?
concepts.lesson: A resource block represents a managed object.

concepts.title: How do you reference a data source named aws_ami.latest?
concepts.lesson: Data source references use the data prefix.

concepts.title: Does reading a data source automatically import the object as a managed resource?
concepts.lesson: Reading data does not bring an object under resource management.

concepts.title: What determines the arguments supported by a resource type?
concepts.lesson: The provider defines the schema and attributes.

concepts.title: Which expression references the output attribute of terraform_data.demo?
concepts.lesson: A reference includes the type, local name, and attribute.

concepts.title: What does referencing another resource attribute usually establish?
concepts.lesson: Terraform infers a dependency from a reference.

concepts.title: How do you reference a local value named env?
concepts.lesson: Local values use the local namespace.

concepts.title: How do you reference an instance of a resource with count at index zero?
concepts.lesson: Count instances are indexed using square brackets.

concepts.title: What can a computed attribute be before apply?
concepts.lesson: Some values are known only after a resource is created.

concepts.title: How do you reference input variable region?
concepts.lesson: Input variables are referenced through var.

concepts.title: Which file name is automatically loaded for input variable values?
concepts.lesson: Terraform automatically loads terraform.tfvars.

concepts.title: Which environment variable sets the input variable region?
concepts.lesson: Input variable environment variables use the TF_VAR_ prefix.

concepts.title: Which block exposes a value from a module?
concepts.lesson: An output exposes a value to the calling module.

concepts.title: What happens when a variable has no default and no supplied value in noninteractive mode?
concepts.lesson: A required input without a value causes an error in non-interactive execution.

concepts.title: Which type represents unique unordered strings?
concepts.lesson: A set contains unique elements with no guaranteed order.

concepts.title: Which type represents an ordered collection of strings?
concepts.lesson: A list preserves order and allows duplicates.

concepts.title: Which type maps string keys to numeric values?
concepts.lesson: A map associates values with keys.

concepts.title: Which type can declare named attributes with different types?
concepts.lesson: An object defines named attributes with types.

concepts.title: Which type describes a fixed sequence of potentially different element types?
concepts.lesson: A tuple has a type for each position.

concepts.title: What does length(["a", "b"]) return?
concepts.lesson: Length returns the number of elements in a collection.

concepts.title: Which meta-argument creates instances keyed by a map?
concepts.lesson: For_each uses map keys or elements of a set of strings.

concepts.title: Which expression accesses the current key in a for_each resource?
concepts.lesson: Each.key contains the current key.

concepts.title: Which expression selects a value conditionally?
concepts.lesson: A conditional expression has the form condition ? true_val : false_val.

concepts.title: Which function combines maps with later values overriding earlier ones?
concepts.lesson: Merge combines maps and prefers later values when keys conflict.

concepts.title: Which lifecycle rule creates a replacement before destruction?
concepts.lesson: The rule changes replacement order if the infrastructure supports it.

concepts.title: Which meta-argument expresses a hidden dependency?
concepts.lesson: Use depends_on when references do not express a dependency.

concepts.title: Which lifecycle rule ignores selected attribute changes during update planning?
concepts.lesson: Ignore_changes allows shared management of selected attributes.

concepts.title: Which lifecycle rule can trigger replacement based on another managed resource change?
concepts.lesson: Replace_triggered_by triggers replacement when a specified change occurs.

concepts.title: Should explicit depends_on replace ordinary attribute references everywhere?
concepts.lesson: Implicit references are usually more precise and preferable.

concepts.title: Which block reports failed assertions as warnings?
concepts.lesson: A check block provides non-blocking condition checks.

concepts.title: Which block can reject an invalid input variable?
concepts.lesson: Validation v variable bloku kontroluje vstup.

concepts.title: Which lifecycle condition checks an assumption before resource operations?
concepts.lesson: A precondition checks an assumption before an operation.

concepts.title: Which lifecycle condition checks a guarantee about resource results?
concepts.lesson: A postcondition checks resulting attributes and can block dependent operations.

concepts.title: Which argument supplies the message for a failed custom condition?
concepts.lesson: Error_message explains the violated condition.

concepts.title: Does sensitive = true alone prevent storage in state?
concepts.lesson: Sensitive hides normal display but does not necessarily remove the value from state.

concepts.title: Which variable setting omits its value from plan and state in supported contexts?
concepts.lesson: Ephemeral values are omitted from plans and state and have restricted usage.

concepts.title: What can a provider-supported write-only argument avoid storing?
concepts.lesson: A write-only argument is not persisted in state or plans.

concepts.title: Which HashiCorp product provides centralized secrets management?
concepts.lesson: Vault manages secrets; retrieving a secret does not guarantee its absence from state.

concepts.title: Should state and saved plans be treated as potentially sensitive?
concepts.lesson: Restrict access to state and plans even when outputs are marked sensitive.

concepts.title: Which source refers to a local module?
concepts.lesson: A relative path beginning with ./ indicates a local module.

concepts.title: Which module argument specifies where to obtain its code?
concepts.lesson: Source specifies the module location.

concepts.title: Can modules be sourced from a Git repository?
concepts.lesson: Terraform supports Git and other module source types.

concepts.title: Which command retrieves child modules during initialization?
concepts.lesson: Init retrieves modules and providers.

concepts.title: Can source normally be computed from an input variable in Terraform 1.12?
concepts.lesson: Source requires a literal value.

concepts.title: How does a parent pass a child module input?
concepts.lesson: A module argument assigns a value to its input variable.

concepts.title: Can a child directly read arbitrary parent local values?
concepts.lesson: Values must be explicitly passed through inputs.

concepts.title: How does a child expose a value to its parent?
concepts.lesson: Outputs form the public interface of a module.

concepts.title: Do root and child module variables share a global namespace?
concepts.lesson: Each module has its own variable scope.

concepts.title: Where are input variables for a child declared?
concepts.lesson: A child module declares its own input interface.

concepts.title: How do you reference output id of module network?
concepts.lesson: Module outputs are referenced using module.NAME.OUTPUT.

concepts.title: Which block calls a child module?
concepts.lesson: A module block references a package of configuration.

concepts.title: Can a module call another child module?
concepts.lesson: Modules can be composed into a hierarchy.

concepts.title: Which meta-argument can create multiple module instances keyed by a map?
concepts.lesson: Modern Terraform supports for_each in module blocks.

concepts.title: What is the root module?
concepts.lesson: The root module is the entry configuration for the current Terraform workflow.

concepts.title: Which argument constrains a Registry module version?
concepts.lesson: Version v module bloku obmedzuje verziu Registry modulu.

concepts.title: How can a Git module source select a tag?
concepts.lesson: Git source podporuje ref pre tag, vetvu alebo commit.

concepts.title: Does .terraform.lock.hcl lock remote module versions?
concepts.lesson: The lock file records providers, not remote module versions.

concepts.title: Which command can update installed modules to allowed newer versions?
concepts.lesson: Init -upgrade updates dependency selection within constraints.

concepts.title: What improves repeatability for a Registry module?
concepts.lesson: An explicit constraint reduces unexpected module changes.

concepts.title: Which backend is the default?
concepts.lesson: Without backend configuration, the local backend is used.

concepts.title: What is the default local state filename for the default workspace?
concepts.lesson: Local backend zapisuje state do terraform.tfstate.

concepts.title: Does the local backend support state locking?
concepts.lesson: The local backend uses operating system locks.

concepts.title: Should local state containing secrets be committed to a public repository?
concepts.lesson: State can contain sensitive information.

concepts.title: What selects the location of local state in a local backend block?
concepts.lesson: The local backend allows a path to be configured.

concepts.title: Why is state locking used?
concepts.lesson: Locking protects against concurrent writes, not disclosure of secrets.

concepts.title: Which command can release a stale lock using its ID?
concepts.lesson: Force-unlock removes a lock when the operation is no longer running.

concepts.title: Should force-unlock be used while another valid apply is running?
concepts.lesson: Removing an active lock can corrupt state.

concepts.title: Which option controls waiting for a state lock?
concepts.lesson: Lock-timeout specifies how long to wait for a lock.

concepts.title: Do all backends necessarily support state locking?
concepts.lesson: Locking support depends on the backend.

concepts.title: Which init option migrates state during backend reconfiguration?
concepts.lesson: Migrate-state transfers state to the new backend.

concepts.title: Where is the backend block declared?
concepts.lesson: A backend belongs in the terraform block.

concepts.title: Can backend configuration directly reference ordinary input variables?
concepts.lesson: The backend is initialized before normal variable evaluation.

concepts.title: Which S3 backend option enables native lockfile-based locking?
concepts.lesson: Terraform 1.12 supports S3 lockfiles.

concepts.title: What is a benefit of a shared remote backend?
concepts.lesson: A remote backend enables shared state with appropriate permissions.

concepts.title: Which planning mode reconciles state with remote changes without changing remote resources?
concepts.lesson: Refresh-only plans updates to state and root outputs to match reality.

concepts.title: What is infrastructure drift?
concepts.lesson: Drift can result from manual changes outside Terraform.

concepts.title: Which block records a resource address rename without recreation solely due to that rename?
concepts.lesson: Moved deklaruje presun adresy state.

concepts.title: Which CLI command removes a binding from state without destroying its remote object?
concepts.lesson: State rm forgets the object; the remote object remains.

concepts.title: Which setting in a removed block preserves the remote object?
concepts.lesson: The destroy=false lifecycle setting in a removed block allows management to stop without destruction.

concepts.title: What does terraform import primarily do?
concepts.lesson: Import associates an existing object with the configuration.

concepts.title: Which block supports declarative import?
concepts.lesson: An import block allows an import to be planned and applied.

concepts.title: Which import block argument identifies the destination resource address?
concepts.lesson: To specifies the resource address; id identifies the object.

concepts.title: Does classic terraform import automatically write the resource configuration?
concepts.lesson: With traditional CLI import, configuration must be prepared separately.

concepts.title: Which plan option can generate configuration for suitable import blocks?
concepts.lesson: Terraform can generate initial HCL that should be reviewed.

concepts.title: Which command lists resource addresses in state?
concepts.lesson: State list displays managed object addresses.

concepts.title: Which command displays attributes of one resource in state?
concepts.lesson: State show displays a specific instance.

concepts.title: Which command retrieves raw state from the configured backend?
concepts.lesson: State pull prints state; handle its output carefully.

concepts.title: Which command displays a saved plan in JSON format?
concepts.lesson: Show -json enables machine processing of a saved plan.

concepts.title: Which command can rename a resource binding imperatively?
concepts.lesson: State mv moves a binding to a new address.

concepts.title: Which environment variable controls logging verbosity?
concepts.lesson: TF_LOG sets the logging level.

concepts.title: Which conventional TF_LOG level is most verbose?
concepts.lesson: TRACE provides the most detailed logs.

concepts.title: Which variable specifies a log file path when logging is enabled?
concepts.lesson: TF_LOG_PATH specifies a file for diagnostic logs.

concepts.title: Can verbose logs contain sensitive information?
concepts.lesson: Protect diagnostic logs and review them before sharing.

concepts.title: Which variable specifically controls provider logging?
concepts.lesson: TF_LOG_PROVIDER allows logging to focus on providers.

concepts.title: What can an HCP Terraform workspace provide?
concepts.lesson: A workspace groups state, configuration, and run workflows.

concepts.title: What can trigger a VCS-driven run?
concepts.lesson: VCS integration can trigger runs based on repository changes.

concepts.title: Which run phase proposes infrastructure changes?
concepts.lesson: Plan prepares changes; apply executes them.

concepts.title: Can HCP Terraform use remote execution?
concepts.lesson: Remote execution runs Terraform on managed infrastructure.

concepts.title: What can a speculative plan support?
concepts.lesson: A speculative plan is for review, not deployment.

concepts.title: Which feature enforces organizational rules on runs?
concepts.lesson: Policies enforce organizational rules according to available features.

concepts.title: Which feature shares reusable input values across workspaces?
concepts.lesson: Variable sets simplify centralized input configuration.

concepts.title: What helps restrict who may approve or manage runs?
concepts.lesson: Team permissions control access to operations.

concepts.title: Which policy language is supported by HashiCorp for policy as code?
concepts.lesson: Sentinel is a policy-as-code language; HCP supports other options as well.

concepts.title: What helps standardize shared modules inside an organization?
concepts.lesson: A private registry allows internal modules to be published and used.

concepts.title: What groups related HCP Terraform workspaces?
concepts.lesson: A project groups workspaces within an organization.

concepts.title: Does each HCP Terraform workspace normally have its own state?
concepts.lesson: A workspace has separate state and settings.

concepts.title: Are CLI workspaces and HCP Terraform workspaces identical concepts?
concepts.lesson: HCP workspaces provide more than state isolation.

concepts.title: Can project-level permissions help organize access?
concepts.lesson: A project provides an organizational boundary for access and management.

concepts.title: What is the top-level grouping containing projects in HCP Terraform?
concepts.lesson: An organization contains projects and workspaces.

concepts.title: Which command obtains HCP Terraform CLI credentials?
concepts.lesson: Login obtains and stores a token for the CLI.

concepts.title: Which terraform block integrates CLI workflow with HCP Terraform?
concepts.lesson: The cloud block defines the organization and workspace selection.

concepts.title: Can a configuration contain both a cloud block and a backend block?
concepts.lesson: Cloud and backend configurations are mutually exclusive.

concepts.title: Which cloud block argument names the HCP Terraform organization?
concepts.lesson: Organization identifies the HCP organization.

concepts.title: Can an existing local state be migrated into HCP Terraform during initialization?
concepts.lesson: Init may offer state migration when switching to cloud integration.
